CreateUnit.title: Spawn a Footman
CreateUnit.description: Create a Footman for Player 1 at the map origin and return the unit. The unit stays in the map until your gameplay removes it.
CreateUnit.usage: Call `ExampleCreateUnit()` after map initialization. Keep the returned unit if another system needs it.

GetUnitX.title: Read a unit’s coordinates
GetUnitX.description: Read the current X and Y coordinates and show them to the unit’s owner.
GetUnitX.usage: Call `ExampleGetUnitX(whichUnit)` with an existing unit after the loading screen.
GetUnitX.jass:
function ExampleGetUnitX takes unit whichUnit returns nothing
    local real x = GetUnitX(whichUnit)
    local real y = GetUnitY(whichUnit)
    call DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(GetOwningPlayer(whichUnit), 0.0, 0.0, 5.0, "X=" + R2S(x) + ", Y=" + R2S(y))
endfunction
GetUnitX.lua:
function ExampleGetUnitX(whichUnit)
    local x = GetUnitX(whichUnit)
    local y = GetUnitY(whichUnit)
    DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(GetOwningPlayer(whichUnit), 0, 0, 5,
        "X=" .. R2S(x) .. ", Y=" .. R2S(y))
end

SetUnitPosition.title: Move a unit to a point
SetUnitPosition.description: Reposition an existing unit to coordinates (256, 256). The engine applies its normal placement and pathing behavior.
SetUnitPosition.usage: Call `ExampleSetUnitPosition(whichUnit)` in a flat test area. Use an order instead when the unit should walk there.
SetUnitPosition.jass:
function ExampleSetUnitPosition takes unit whichUnit returns nothing
    call SetUnitPosition(whichUnit, 256.0, 256.0)
endfunction

SetUnitState.title: Heal a living unit
SetUnitState.description: Add 50 life to a living unit, capped at its current maximum life.
SetUnitState.usage: Call `ExampleSetUnitState(whichUnit)` with a living unit. This is healing, not a resurrection routine.
SetUnitState.jass:
function ExampleSetUnitState takes unit whichUnit returns nothing
    local real maximum = GetUnitState(whichUnit, UNIT_STATE_MAX_LIFE)
    local real healed = GetUnitState(whichUnit, UNIT_STATE_LIFE) + 50.0
    if healed > maximum then
        set healed = maximum
    endif
    call SetUnitState(whichUnit, UNIT_STATE_LIFE, healed)
endfunction
SetUnitState.lua:
function ExampleSetUnitState(whichUnit)
    local maximum = GetUnitState(whichUnit, UNIT_STATE_MAX_LIFE)
    local healed = GetUnitState(whichUnit, UNIT_STATE_LIFE) + 50.0
    if healed > maximum then
        healed = maximum
    end
    SetUnitState(whichUnit, UNIT_STATE_LIFE, healed)
end

SetUnitOwner.title: Transfer a unit to Player 2
SetUnitOwner.description: Change an existing unit’s owner to Player 2 and update its team color. Player indices start at zero.
SetUnitOwner.jass:
function ExampleSetUnitOwner takes unit whichUnit returns nothing
    call SetUnitOwner(whichUnit, Player(1), true)
endfunction

UnitAddAbility.title: Give a unit a custom ability
UnitAddAbility.description: Add an existing custom ability and return whether adding it succeeded.
UnitAddAbility.usage: Replace `A000` with your map’s ability code, then call `ExampleUnitAddAbility(whichUnit)`. The object must already exist in the map.

SetUnitAbilityLevel.title: Set an ability to level 2
SetUnitAbilityLevel.description: Set a unit’s custom ability to level 2 and return the level reported by the engine.
SetUnitAbilityLevel.usage: Replace `A000`; give the unit that ability first and configure it with at least two levels. Call `ExampleSetUnitAbilityLevel(whichUnit)`.

IssuePointOrder.title: Order a unit to walk
IssuePointOrder.description: Issue a move order toward coordinates (512, 256) and return whether the engine accepted the order.
IssuePointOrder.usage: Call `ExampleIssuePointOrder(whichUnit)` with a controllable unit in a passable test area.

IssueTargetOrder.title: Order an attack on a target
IssueTargetOrder.description: Issue an attack order against another unit. The attacker must be able to attack that target.
IssueTargetOrder.usage: Call `ExampleIssueTargetOrder(attacker, target)` with two existing units. An accepted order does not guarantee the target is reachable.

IssueImmediateOrder.title: Stop a unit
IssueImmediateOrder.description: Issue the immediate stop order, which does not take a target or coordinates.
IssueImmediateOrder.usage: Call `ExampleIssueImmediateOrder(whichUnit)` to interrupt the unit’s current order.

CreateItem.title: Place a healing potion
CreateItem.description: Create a healing potion on the ground at coordinates (128, 128).
CreateItem.usage: Call `ExampleCreateItem()` after initialization. The returned item stays in the map; remove it later if your system owns its lifetime.

UnitAddItemById.title: Give a unit a charged potion
UnitAddItemById.description: Create a healing potion for a unit with inventory and set its charges to three. Check that an item was returned before editing it.
UnitAddItemById.usage: Call `ExampleUnitAddItemById(whichUnit)` with a hero or another unit that has inventory. Test full-inventory behavior in your map.
UnitAddItemById.jass:
function ExampleUnitAddItemById takes unit whichUnit returns nothing
    local item potion = UnitAddItemById(whichUnit, 'phea')
    if potion != null then
        call SetItemCharges(potion, 3)
    endif
    set potion = null
endfunction
UnitAddItemById.lua:
function ExampleUnitAddItemById(whichUnit)
    local potion = UnitAddItemById(whichUnit, FourCC("phea"))
    if potion ~= nil then
        SetItemCharges(potion, 3)
    end
end

SetItemCharges.title: Change an item’s charges
SetItemCharges.description: Set an existing item’s charge count to five. Its object data determines how charges are consumed.
SetItemCharges.usage: Call `ExampleSetItemCharges(whichItem)` with an item configured to use charges.
SetItemCharges.jass:
function ExampleSetItemCharges takes item whichItem returns nothing
    call SetItemCharges(whichItem, 5)
endfunction

RemoveItem.title: Remove an item you own
RemoveItem.description: Remove an item from the game. The helper accepts a missing item without doing anything.
RemoveItem.usage: Call `ExampleRemoveItem(whichItem)`, then clear any stored reference your system keeps to that item.
RemoveItem.jass:
function ExampleRemoveItem takes item whichItem returns nothing
    if whichItem != null then
        call RemoveItem(whichItem)
    endif
endfunction
RemoveItem.lua:
function ExampleRemoveItem(whichItem)
    if whichItem ~= nil then
        RemoveItem(whichItem)
    end
end

TimerStart.title: Run code once after a delay
TimerStart.description: Start a one-shot timer that shows a message after two seconds. Destroy the expired timer inside its callback.
TimerStart.jass:
function ExampleTimerStartElapsed takes nothing returns nothing
    local timer expired = GetExpiredTimer()
    call DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(Player(0), 0.0, 0.0, 5.0, "Two seconds elapsed.")
    call DestroyTimer(expired)
    set expired = null
endfunction

function ExampleTimerStart takes nothing returns nothing
    local timer delayed = CreateTimer()
    call TimerStart(delayed, 2.0, false, function ExampleTimerStartElapsed)
    set delayed = null
endfunction
TimerStart.lua:
function ExampleTimerStart()
    local delayed = CreateTimer()
    TimerStart(delayed, 2.0, false, function()
        DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(Player(0), 0, 0, 5, "Two seconds elapsed.")
        DestroyTimer(delayed)
    end)
end

CreateTimer.title: Start and stop a periodic timer
CreateTimer.description: Keep one timer for a repeating heartbeat. The start function is idempotent; the stop function pauses, destroys and clears the owned timer.
CreateTimer.usage: Call `ExampleCreateTimer()` to start and `ExampleStopHeartbeat()` when the system ends. This recipe owns one shared heartbeat timer.
CreateTimer.jass:
globals
    timer ExampleHeartbeatTimer = null
endglobals

function ExampleHeartbeatTick takes nothing returns nothing
    call DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(Player(0), 0.0, 0.0, 2.0, "Heartbeat")
endfunction

function ExampleCreateTimer takes nothing returns nothing
    if ExampleHeartbeatTimer == null then
        set ExampleHeartbeatTimer = CreateTimer()
        call TimerStart(ExampleHeartbeatTimer, 2.0, true, function ExampleHeartbeatTick)
    endif
endfunction

function ExampleStopHeartbeat takes nothing returns nothing
    if ExampleHeartbeatTimer != null then
        call PauseTimer(ExampleHeartbeatTimer)
        call DestroyTimer(ExampleHeartbeatTimer)
        set ExampleHeartbeatTimer = null
    endif
endfunction
CreateTimer.lua:
local heartbeatTimer = nil

function ExampleCreateTimer()
    if heartbeatTimer ~= nil then
        return
    end
    heartbeatTimer = CreateTimer()
    TimerStart(heartbeatTimer, 2.0, true, function()
        DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(Player(0), 0, 0, 2, "Heartbeat")
    end)
end

function ExampleStopHeartbeat()
    if heartbeatTimer ~= nil then
        PauseTimer(heartbeatTimer)
        DestroyTimer(heartbeatTimer)
        heartbeatTimer = nil
    end
end

GetExpiredTimer.title: Find the timer in its callback
GetExpiredTimer.description: Get the timer responsible for the current timer callback and release it. Event-response values belong to their event context.
GetExpiredTimer.usage: Call `ExampleGetExpiredTimer()` after initialization. Use `GetExpiredTimer()` inside the registered callback, not arbitrary map code.
GetExpiredTimer.jass:
function ExampleExpiredTimerAction takes nothing returns nothing
    local timer expired = GetExpiredTimer()
    call DestroyTimer(expired)
    set expired = null
endfunction

function ExampleGetExpiredTimer takes nothing returns nothing
    local timer delayed = CreateTimer()
    call TimerStart(delayed, 1.0, false, function ExampleExpiredTimerAction)
    set delayed = null
endfunction
GetExpiredTimer.lua:
function ExampleGetExpiredTimer()
    local delayed = CreateTimer()
    TimerStart(delayed, 1.0, false, function()
        local expired = GetExpiredTimer()
        DestroyTimer(expired)
    end)
end

DestroyTimer.title: Release a timer owned by your system
DestroyTimer.description: Pause and destroy an owned timer. Destroying it prevents further periodic callbacks.
DestroyTimer.usage: Call `ExampleDestroyTimer(ownedTimer)` only for a timer your system owns, then clear your stored reference.
DestroyTimer.jass:
function ExampleDestroyTimer takes timer ownedTimer returns nothing
    if ownedTimer != null then
        call PauseTimer(ownedTimer)
        call DestroyTimer(ownedTimer)
    endif
endfunction
DestroyTimer.lua:
function ExampleDestroyTimer(ownedTimer)
    if ownedTimer ~= nil then
        PauseTimer(ownedTimer)
        DestroyTimer(ownedTimer)
    end
end

TriggerRegisterTimerEvent.title: Run a one-shot timed trigger
TriggerRegisterTimerEvent.description: Register a trigger for a single five-second timer event. The action destroys its trigger after showing a message.
TriggerRegisterTimerEvent.usage: Call `ExampleTriggerRegisterTimerEvent()` once after initialization. Unlike the periodic heartbeat recipe, this trigger cleans itself up.
TriggerRegisterTimerEvent.jass:
function ExampleTimedTriggerAction takes nothing returns nothing
    local trigger fired = GetTriggeringTrigger()
    call DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(Player(0), 0.0, 0.0, 5.0, "Timed trigger fired.")
    call DestroyTrigger(fired)
    set fired = null
endfunction

function ExampleTriggerRegisterTimerEvent takes nothing returns nothing
    local trigger timed = CreateTrigger()
    call TriggerRegisterTimerEvent(timed, 5.0, false)
    call TriggerAddAction(timed, function ExampleTimedTriggerAction)
    set timed = null
endfunction
TriggerRegisterTimerEvent.lua:
function ExampleTriggerRegisterTimerEvent()
    local timed = CreateTrigger()
    TriggerRegisterTimerEvent(timed, 5.0, false)
    TriggerAddAction(timed, function()
        DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(Player(0), 0, 0, 5, "Timed trigger fired.")
        DestroyTrigger(timed)
    end)
end

GetSpellAbilityId.title: React to a specific spell
GetSpellAbilityId.description: Register spell-effect events and filter the action by ability raw code. Casting other abilities does not run the custom behavior.
GetSpellAbilityId.usage: Replace `A000` with your custom ability’s raw code, then call `ExampleGetSpellAbilityId()` once after initialization. This registers a map-lifetime trigger.
GetSpellAbilityId.jass:
function ExampleGetSpellAbilityIdAction takes nothing returns nothing
    if GetSpellAbilityId() == 'A000' then
        call DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(GetOwningPlayer(GetTriggerUnit()), 0.0, 0.0, 5.0, "Custom spell cast!")
    endif
endfunction

function ExampleGetSpellAbilityId takes nothing returns nothing
    local trigger spell = CreateTrigger()
    local integer index = 0
    loop
        exitwhen index >= bj_MAX_PLAYER_SLOTS
        call TriggerRegisterPlayerUnitEvent(spell, Player(index), EVENT_PLAYER_UNIT_SPELL_EFFECT, null)
        set index = index + 1
    endloop
    call TriggerAddAction(spell, function ExampleGetSpellAbilityIdAction)
    set spell = null
endfunction
GetSpellAbilityId.lua:
function ExampleGetSpellAbilityId()
    local spell = CreateTrigger()
    for index = 0, bj_MAX_PLAYER_SLOTS - 1 do
        TriggerRegisterPlayerUnitEvent(spell, Player(index),
            EVENT_PLAYER_UNIT_SPELL_EFFECT, nil)
    end
    TriggerAddAction(spell, function()
        if GetSpellAbilityId() ~= FourCC("A000") then
            return
        end
        DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(GetOwningPlayer(GetTriggerUnit()), 0, 0, 5,
            "Custom spell cast!")
    end)
end

GetSpellTargetUnit.title: Damage a spell’s unit target
GetSpellTargetUnit.description: Inside the spell-effect action, capture the caster and unit target before applying 50 magic damage. A point-target spell may have no unit target. This adds damage on top of any effect the base spell already applies.
GetSpellTargetUnit.usage: Replace `A000` with your custom ability’s raw code, then call `ExampleGetSpellTargetUnit()` once after initialization. This registers a map-lifetime trigger.
GetSpellTargetUnit.jass:
function ExampleGetSpellTargetUnitAction takes nothing returns nothing
    local unit caster = GetTriggerUnit()
    local unit target = GetSpellTargetUnit()
    if GetSpellAbilityId() == 'A000' and target != null then
        call UnitDamageTarget(caster, target, 50.0, false, false, ATTACK_TYPE_NORMAL, DAMAGE_TYPE_MAGIC, WEAPON_TYPE_WHOKNOWS)
    endif
    set caster = null
    set target = null
endfunction

function ExampleGetSpellTargetUnit takes nothing returns nothing
    local trigger spell = CreateTrigger()
    local integer index = 0
    loop
        exitwhen index >= bj_MAX_PLAYER_SLOTS
        call TriggerRegisterPlayerUnitEvent(spell, Player(index), EVENT_PLAYER_UNIT_SPELL_EFFECT, null)
        set index = index + 1
    endloop
    call TriggerAddAction(spell, function ExampleGetSpellTargetUnitAction)
    set spell = null
endfunction
GetSpellTargetUnit.lua:
function ExampleGetSpellTargetUnit()
    local spell = CreateTrigger()
    for index = 0, bj_MAX_PLAYER_SLOTS - 1 do
        TriggerRegisterPlayerUnitEvent(spell, Player(index),
            EVENT_PLAYER_UNIT_SPELL_EFFECT, nil)
    end
    TriggerAddAction(spell, function()

TriggerRegisterPlayerUnitEvent.title: React when a unit dies
TriggerRegisterPlayerUnitEvent.description: Register a death event for every player slot and report the dying unit’s name to its owner. Read the event response inside the action.
TriggerRegisterPlayerUnitEvent.usage: Call `ExampleTriggerRegisterPlayerUnitEvent()` once after initialization. The trigger stays active for the map’s lifetime.
TriggerRegisterPlayerUnitEvent.jass:
function ExampleUnitDeathAction takes nothing returns nothing
    local unit dying = GetDyingUnit()
    call DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(GetOwningPlayer(dying), 0.0, 0.0, 5.0, GetUnitName(dying) + " died.")

endfunction

function ExampleTriggerRegisterPlayerUnitEvent takes nothing returns nothing
    local trigger deaths = CreateTrigger()

    loop

        call TriggerRegisterPlayerUnitEvent(deaths, Player(index), EVENT_PLAYER_UNIT_DEATH, null)

GroupEnumUnitsInRange.title: Order nearby friendly units
GroupEnumUnitsInRange.description: Enumerate units within 400 of the origin, issue a move order to Player 1’s units, and destroy the temporary group. Remove each unit before the next iteration.
GroupEnumUnitsInRange.usage: Call `ExampleGroupEnumUnitsInRange()` in a flat test map with Player 1 units near the origin.
GroupEnumUnitsInRange.jass:
function ExampleGroupEnumUnitsInRange takes nothing returns nothing
    local group nearby = CreateGroup()
    local unit current = null
    call GroupEnumUnitsInRange(nearby, 0.0, 0.0, 400.0, null)
    loop
        set current = FirstOfGroup(nearby)
        exitwhen current == null
        call GroupRemoveUnit(nearby, current)
        if GetOwningPlayer(current) == Player(0) then
            call IssuePointOrder(current, "move", 512.0, 0.0)
        endif
    endloop
    call DestroyGroup(nearby)
    set nearby = null
    set current = null
endfunction
GroupEnumUnitsInRange.lua:
function ExampleGroupEnumUnitsInRange()
    local nearby = CreateGroup()
    GroupEnumUnitsInRange(nearby, 0.0, 0.0, 400.0, nil)
    while true do
        local current = FirstOfGroup(nearby)
        if current == nil then
            break
        end
        GroupRemoveUnit(nearby, current)
        if GetOwningPlayer(current) == Player(0) then
            IssuePointOrder(current, "move", 512.0, 0.0)
        end
    end
    DestroyGroup(nearby)
end

ForGroup.title: Stop all of Player 1’s units
ForGroup.description: Use a group callback and GetEnumUnit to issue an order to every enumerated unit, then release the group.
ForGroup.usage: Call `ExampleForGroup()` after initialization. `GetEnumUnit()` is used only inside the callback.
ForGroup.jass:
function ExampleStopEnumUnit takes nothing returns nothing
    call IssueImmediateOrder(GetEnumUnit(), "stop")
endfunction

function ExampleForGroup takes nothing returns nothing
    local group owned = CreateGroup()
    call GroupEnumUnitsOfPlayer(owned, Player(0), null)
    call ForGroup(owned, function ExampleStopEnumUnit)
    call DestroyGroup(owned)
    set owned = null
endfunction
ForGroup.lua:
function ExampleForGroup()
    local owned = CreateGroup()
    GroupEnumUnitsOfPlayer(owned, Player(0), nil)
    ForGroup(owned, function()
        IssueImmediateOrder(GetEnumUnit(), "stop")
    end)
    DestroyGroup(owned)
end

DestroyGroup.title: Count a group and release it
DestroyGroup.description: Create a temporary group, count the units near the origin, and destroy the group. Destroying the group does not remove its units.
DestroyGroup.usage: Call `ExampleDestroyGroup()` after the loading screen to see the count.
DestroyGroup.jass:
function ExampleDestroyGroup takes nothing returns nothing
    local group nearby = CreateGroup()
    local integer count = 0
    call GroupEnumUnitsInRange(nearby, 0.0, 0.0, 400.0, null)
    set count = BlzGroupGetSize(nearby)
    call DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(Player(0), 0.0, 0.0, 5.0, "Nearby units: " + I2S(count))
    call DestroyGroup(nearby)
    set nearby = null
endfunction
DestroyGroup.lua:
function ExampleDestroyGroup()
    local nearby = CreateGroup()
    GroupEnumUnitsInRange(nearby, 0.0, 0.0, 400.0, nil)
    local count = BlzGroupGetSize(nearby)
    DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(Player(0), 0, 0, 5, "Nearby units: " .. I2S(count))
    DestroyGroup(nearby)
end

UnitDamageTarget.title: Apply spell damage to a unit
UnitDamageTarget.description: Apply 75 magic damage from a source unit to a target. This call can fire damage events in other systems.
UnitDamageTarget.usage: Call `ExampleUnitDamageTarget(source, target)` with two existing units. Avoid calling it unconditionally inside a damage event, which can recurse.

AddSpecialEffect.title: Play a one-shot effect at a point

AddSpecialEffect.jass:
function ExampleAddSpecialEffect takes real x, real y returns nothing
    local effect visual = AddSpecialEffect("Abilities\\Spells\\Human\\HolyBolt\\HolyBoltSpecialArt.mdl", x, y)
    call DestroyEffect(visual)
    set visual = null
endfunction

function ExampleAddSpecialEffect(x, y)

AddSpecialEffectTarget.usage: Store the result of `ExampleAddSpecialEffectTarget(whichUnit)` and call `DestroyEffect` when your visual ends. This helper intentionally leaves that effect alive.

DestroyEffect.title: Remove an owned effect

DestroyEffect.jass:

    if visual != null then

end

Rect.title: Find the center of a temporary area
Rect.description: Create a rectangle, read its center coordinates, and remove it after use. The rectangle is a geometry handle; it is not a region event by itself.
Rect.usage: Call `ExampleRect()` after the loading screen to display the center.

    local rect area = Rect(-128.0, -256.0, 128.0, 256.0)

    call DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(Player(0), 0.0, 0.0, 5.0, "Center: " + R2S(x) + ", " + R2S(y))
    call RemoveRect(area)
    set area = null
endfunction

function ExampleRect()
    local area = Rect(-128.0, -256.0, 128.0, 256.0)

end

TriggerRegisterEnterRegion.title: Watch units entering an area
TriggerRegisterEnterRegion.description: Create an entry region and report units that enter it. The setup owns its region and trigger; the stop function destroys the trigger before removing the region.
TriggerRegisterEnterRegion.usage: Call `ExampleTriggerRegisterEnterRegion()` once, then move a unit into the area from outside. Call `ExampleStopEntryRegion()` to stop watching.
TriggerRegisterEnterRegion.jass:
globals
    region ExampleEntryRegion = null
    trigger ExampleEntryTrigger = null
endglobals

function ExampleEntryAction takes nothing returns nothing
    local unit entering = GetEnteringUnit()
    call DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(GetOwningPlayer(entering), 0.0, 0.0, 5.0, "Entered the area.")
    set entering = null
endfunction

function ExampleTriggerRegisterEnterRegion takes nothing returns nothing
    local rect area = null
    if ExampleEntryTrigger != null then
        return
    endif
    set area = Rect(0.0, 0.0, 512.0, 512.0)
    set ExampleEntryRegion = CreateRegion()
    call RegionAddRect(ExampleEntryRegion, area)
    call RemoveRect(area)
    set area = null
    set ExampleEntryTrigger = CreateTrigger()
    call TriggerRegisterEnterRegion(ExampleEntryTrigger, ExampleEntryRegion, null)
    call TriggerAddAction(ExampleEntryTrigger, function ExampleEntryAction)
endfunction

function ExampleStopEntryRegion takes nothing returns nothing
    if ExampleEntryTrigger != null then
        call DestroyTrigger(ExampleEntryTrigger)
        set ExampleEntryTrigger = null
        call RemoveRegion(ExampleEntryRegion)
        set ExampleEntryRegion = null
    endif
endfunction
TriggerRegisterEnterRegion.lua:
local entryRegion = nil
local entryTrigger = nil

function ExampleTriggerRegisterEnterRegion()
    if entryTrigger ~= nil then
        return
    end
    local area = Rect(0.0, 0.0, 512.0, 512.0)
    entryRegion = CreateRegion()
    RegionAddRect(entryRegion, area)
    RemoveRect(area)
    entryTrigger = CreateTrigger()
    TriggerRegisterEnterRegion(entryTrigger, entryRegion, nil)
    TriggerAddAction(entryTrigger, function()
        local entering = GetEnteringUnit()
        DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(GetOwningPlayer(entering), 0, 0, 5,
            "Entered the area.")
    end)
end

function ExampleStopEntryRegion()
    if entryTrigger ~= nil then
        DestroyTrigger(entryTrigger)
        entryTrigger = nil
        RemoveRegion(entryRegion)
        entryRegion = nil
    end
end

Player.title: Use zero-based player indices
Player.description: Return Player 1’s player handle. The zero-based index identifies a slot; it does not tell you whether a human is playing there.
Player.usage: Use `ExamplePlayer()` wherever you need the Player 1 handle.

DisplayTimedTextToPlayer.title: Show a welcome message after loading
DisplayTimedTextToPlayer.description: Delay a message by one second so it can appear after the loading screen, then release the one-shot timer.
DisplayTimedTextToPlayer.usage: Call `ExampleDisplayTimedTextToPlayer()` once after initialization. The message is sent to Player 1.
DisplayTimedTextToPlayer.jass:
function ExampleWelcomeMessage takes nothing returns nothing
    call DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(Player(0), 0.0, 0.0, 10.0, "Hello, map maker!")
    call DestroyTimer(GetExpiredTimer())
endfunction

function ExampleDisplayTimedTextToPlayer takes nothing returns nothing
    local timer delayed = CreateTimer()
    call TimerStart(delayed, 1.0, false, function ExampleWelcomeMessage)
    set delayed = null
endfunction
DisplayTimedTextToPlayer.lua:
function ExampleDisplayTimedTextToPlayer()
    local delayed = CreateTimer()
    TimerStart(delayed, 1.0, false, function()
        DisplayTimedTextToPlayer(Player(0), 0, 0, 10, "Hello, map maker!")
        DestroyTimer(delayed)
    end)
end

SetPlayerState.title: Give Player 1 bonus gold
SetPlayerState.description: Add 100 gold to Player 1’s current gold instead of replacing the balance with 100.
SetPlayerState.usage: Call `ExampleSetPlayerState()` from synchronized gameplay code. Do not run this gameplay change only for a local client.
SetPlayerState.jass:
function ExampleSetPlayerState takes nothing returns nothing
    local player recipient = Player(0)
    local integer currentGold = GetPlayerState(recipient, PLAYER_STATE_RESOURCE_GOLD)
    call SetPlayerState(recipient, PLAYER_STATE_RESOURCE_GOLD, currentGold + 100)
    set recipient = null
endfunction
SetPlayerState.lua:
function ExampleSetPlayerState()
    local recipient = Player(0)
    local currentGold = GetPlayerState(recipient, PLAYER_STATE_RESOURCE_GOLD)
    SetPlayerState(recipient, PLAYER_STATE_RESOURCE_GOLD, currentGold + 100)
end

SetPlayerAlliance.title: Make a mutual passive alliance
SetPlayerAlliance.description: Set passive alliance in both directions between Player 1 and Player 2. Shared vision and shared control use separate alliance flags.
SetPlayerAlliance.usage: Call `ExampleSetPlayerAlliance()` from synchronized gameplay code when the alliance should change.
SetPlayerAlliance.jass:
function ExampleSetPlayerAlliance takes nothing returns nothing
    call SetPlayerAlliance(Player(0), Player(1), ALLIANCE_PASSIVE, true)
    call SetPlayerAlliance(Player(1), Player(0), ALLIANCE_PASSIVE, true)
endfunction
SetPlayerAlliance.lua:
function ExampleSetPlayerAlliance()
    SetPlayerAlliance(Player(0), Player(1), ALLIANCE_PASSIVE, true)
    SetPlayerAlliance(Player(1), Player(0), ALLIANCE_PASSIVE, true)
end

CreateQuest.title: Create and complete a quest
CreateQuest.description: Own a single quest, mark it completed when its objective finishes, and optionally remove it from the quest log.
CreateQuest.usage: Call `ExampleCreateQuest()` once, `ExampleCompleteQuest()` when the objective is met, and `ExampleRemoveQuest()` if the quest should be removed.
CreateQuest.jass:
globals
    quest ExampleQuest = null
endglobals

function ExampleCreateQuest takes nothing returns nothing
    if ExampleQuest == null then
        set ExampleQuest = CreateQuest()
        call QuestSetTitle(ExampleQuest, "Defend the village")
        call QuestSetDescription(ExampleQuest, "Defeat the attacking wave.")
        call QuestSetRequired(ExampleQuest, true)
    endif
endfunction

function ExampleCompleteQuest takes nothing returns nothing
    if ExampleQuest != null then
        call QuestSetCompleted(ExampleQuest, true)
    endif
endfunction

function ExampleRemoveQuest takes nothing returns nothing
    if ExampleQuest != null then
        call DestroyQuest(ExampleQuest)
        set ExampleQuest = null
    endif
endfunction
CreateQuest.lua:
local villageQuest = nil

function ExampleCreateQuest()
    if villageQuest == nil then
        villageQuest = CreateQuest()
        QuestSetTitle(villageQuest, "Defend the village")
        QuestSetDescription(villageQuest, "Defeat the attacking wave.")
        QuestSetRequired(villageQuest, true)
    end
end

function ExampleCompleteQuest()
    if villageQuest ~= nil then
        QuestSetCompleted(villageQuest, true)
    end
end

function ExampleRemoveQuest()
    if villageQuest ~= nil then
        DestroyQuest(villageQuest)
        villageQuest = nil
    end
end

InitHashtable.title: Initialize shared per-unit storage
InitHashtable.description: Create one map-lifetime hashtable and store an integer under a unit’s handle ID. Clear that unit’s entries when your system stops tracking it.
InitHashtable.usage: Call `ExampleInitHashtable(whichUnit)` with an existing unit. Call `ExampleForgetStoredUnit(whichUnit)` before removing that tracked unit.
InitHashtable.jass:
globals
    hashtable ExampleUnitData = null
endglobals

function ExampleInitHashtable takes unit whichUnit returns nothing
    if ExampleUnitData == null then
        set ExampleUnitData = InitHashtable()
    endif
    call SaveInteger(ExampleUnitData, GetHandleId(whichUnit), 0, 3)
endfunction

function ExampleForgetStoredUnit takes unit whichUnit returns nothing
    if ExampleUnitData != null then
        call FlushChildHashtable(ExampleUnitData, GetHandleId(whichUnit))
    endif
endfunction
InitHashtable.lua:
local unitData = nil

function ExampleInitHashtable(whichUnit)
    if unitData == nil then
        unitData = InitHashtable()
    end
    SaveInteger(unitData, GetHandleId(whichUnit), 0, 3)
end

function ExampleForgetStoredUnit(whichUnit)
    if unitData ~= nil then
        FlushChildHashtable(unitData, GetHandleId(whichUnit))
    end
end

SaveInteger.title: Store an integer for a unit
SaveInteger.description: Store the value 5 under a unit’s handle ID and child key 0 in a hashtable supplied by your system.
SaveInteger.usage: Call `ExampleSaveInteger(data, whichUnit)` with an initialized hashtable and an existing unit. Clear the entries before the tracked unit is removed.
SaveInteger.jass:
function ExampleSaveInteger takes hashtable data, unit whichUnit returns nothing
    call SaveInteger(data, GetHandleId(whichUnit), 0, 5)
endfunction

LoadInteger.title: Read a unit’s stored integer
LoadInteger.description: Read the same parent and child keys used by the SaveInteger recipe.
LoadInteger.usage: Call `ExampleLoadInteger(data, whichUnit)` with the same table and unit you saved. Use the returned integer in your system.

FlushChildHashtable.title: Forget one unit’s stored data
FlushChildHashtable.description: Clear all child entries under one unit’s handle ID while leaving other units’ entries in the table.
FlushChildHashtable.usage: Call `ExampleFlushChildHashtable(data, whichUnit)` before removing the tracked unit. This clears entries; it does not destroy the hashtable.
FlushChildHashtable.jass:
function ExampleFlushChildHashtable takes hashtable data, unit whichUnit returns nothing
    call FlushChildHashtable(data, GetHandleId(whichUnit))
endfunction

RemoveUnit.title: Release a temporary unit
RemoveUnit.description: Remove a unit when the system that created it has finished using it.
RemoveUnit.usage: Pass a valid temporary unit owned by your system. After this call, clear any stored references to that unit; do not pass an unrelated map unit.
RemoveUnit.jass:
function ExampleRemoveUnit takes unit ownedUnit returns nothing
    if ownedUnit != null then
        call RemoveUnit(ownedUnit)
    endif
endfunction
RemoveUnit.lua:
function ExampleRemoveUnit(ownedUnit)
    if ownedUnit ~= nil then
        RemoveUnit(ownedUnit)
    end
end

GroupClear.title: Reuse an empty group
GroupClear.description: Clear membership, then reuse the same group before releasing it. Neither clearing nor destroying the group removes its units.
GroupClear.usage: Pass a valid existing unit. The example owns its scratch group and releases it before returning.
GroupClear.jass:
function ExampleGroupClear takes unit whichUnit returns nothing
    local group scratch = CreateGroup()
    call GroupAddUnit(scratch, whichUnit)
    call GroupClear(scratch)
    call GroupAddUnit(scratch, whichUnit)
    call DestroyGroup(scratch)
    set scratch = null
endfunction
GroupClear.lua:
function ExampleGroupClear(whichUnit)
    local scratch = CreateGroup()
    GroupAddUnit(scratch, whichUnit)
    GroupClear(scratch)
    GroupAddUnit(scratch, whichUnit)
    DestroyGroup(scratch)
end

GetTriggerUnit.title: Read the unit from a death event
GetTriggerUnit.description: Register a map-lifetime death listener and read its event unit in the action. The Blizzard helper registers the event across player slots.
GetTriggerUnit.usage: Call ExampleGetTriggerUnit once during map initialization. Keep the trigger for the map lifetime; repeatedly registering it would duplicate messages.
GetTriggerUnit.jass:
function ExampleTriggerUnitDeathAction takes nothing returns nothing
    local unit eventUnit = GetTriggerUnit()
    call DisplayTextToPlayer(GetOwningPlayer(eventUnit), 0, 0, GetUnitName(eventUnit) + " died.")
    set eventUnit = null
endfunction

function ExampleGetTriggerUnit takes nothing returns nothing
    local trigger listener = CreateTrigger()
    call TriggerRegisterAnyUnitEventBJ(listener, EVENT_PLAYER_UNIT_DEATH)
    call TriggerAddAction(listener, function ExampleTriggerUnitDeathAction)
    set listener = null
endfunction
GetTriggerUnit.lua:
function ExampleGetTriggerUnit()
    local listener = CreateTrigger()
    TriggerRegisterAnyUnitEventBJ(listener, EVENT_PLAYER_UNIT_DEATH)
    TriggerAddAction(listener, function()
        local eventUnit = GetTriggerUnit()
        DisplayTextToPlayer(GetOwningPlayer(eventUnit), 0, 0, GetUnitName(eventUnit) .. " died.")
    end)
end

DestroyTrigger.title: Release a temporary trigger
DestroyTrigger.description: Destroy an owned listener once its events and actions are no longer needed.
DestroyTrigger.usage: Pass a trigger retained by your system. Release any separately owned timers, groups or locations as well, and clear the caller's stored trigger reference afterwards.
DestroyTrigger.jass:
function ExampleDestroyTrigger takes trigger ownedTrigger returns nothing
    if ownedTrigger != null then
        call DestroyTrigger(ownedTrigger)
    endif
endfunction
DestroyTrigger.lua:
function ExampleDestroyTrigger(ownedTrigger)
    if ownedTrigger ~= nil then
        DestroyTrigger(ownedTrigger)
    end
end

GetUnitLoc.title: Read and release a unit position
GetUnitLoc.description: Read a snapshot of a unit's position through a temporary location and release that location after extracting its coordinates.
GetUnitLoc.usage: Pass a valid existing unit. If you need only coordinates in your own code, prefer GetUnitX and GetUnitY to avoid allocating a location.
GetUnitLoc.jass:
function ExampleGetUnitLoc takes unit whichUnit returns nothing
    local location point = GetUnitLoc(whichUnit)
    local real x = GetLocationX(point)
    local real y = GetLocationY(point)
    call RemoveLocation(point)
    set point = null
    call DisplayTextToPlayer(Player(0), 0, 0, R2S(x) + ", " + R2S(y))
endfunction
GetUnitLoc.lua:
function ExampleGetUnitLoc(whichUnit)
    local point = GetUnitLoc(whichUnit)
    local x = GetLocationX(point)
    local y = GetLocationY(point)
    RemoveLocation(point)
    DisplayTextToPlayer(Player(0), 0, 0, tostring(x) .. ", " .. tostring(y))
end
